approvedChanges.question: CHG-unified-declarative-quality-pack-contract
approvedChanges.currentState: Production loops use versioned quality graph objects in src while lab candidates define related graph structures separately. Dependencies now execute as a DAG, but pack identity, rollout policy, evidence adapters, and production/lab composition are not governed by one declarative contract.

approvedChanges.rationale: A shared declarative contract removes production/lab drift and creates the safe substrate required for constrained project policies and the future Quality Designer skill.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Creates predictable, inspectable quality behavior and safer future project customization.
approvedChanges.maintainerImpact: Replaces parallel production/lab graph definitions with one validated pack contract and explicit rollout semantics.
approvedChanges.recommendationRationale: This is the smallest architecture step that unlocks constrained project policies without weakening kernel authority or evaluation independence.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: User explicitly approved proceeding with the declarative quality-pack foundation.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Reduces graph drift, preserves independent evaluation, and creates a testable extension boundary.

approvedChanges.desiredOutcome: Built-in production graphs and lab candidates compose validated declarative packs through the same parser and scheduler while kernel standards remain immutable.
approvedChanges.successSignal: Production and lab load the same versioned schema; unknown keys, duplicate ids, invalid layers/dependencies, cycles, unsupported evaluators/adapters, and kernel overrides fail closed; observe mode records evidence without changing exits; current DEC/PEC/IEC/PCE behavior remains green.

approvedChanges.question: CHG-dashboard-live-trace-recovery
approvedChanges.currentState: The dashboard opens an EventSource and receives initial state, but EventSource errors only change status text. Polling starts only if the EventSource constructor throws, which browsers normally do not do. A missed watch broadcast or disconnected stream can therefore leave an open dashboard stale indefinitely.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Trace appends stream over SSE within the existing debounce window and the browser also polls current state every second as a recovery guarantee, so progress catches up automatically without reload or reopen.
approvedChanges.rationale: A trace-first progress surface is useful only when durable agent trace changes become visible immediately and stale streams self-heal.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Agent trace progress appears live in the dashboard and recovers automatically from transient stream failures.

approvedChanges.routeRationale: Bounded browser refresh and focused runtime test need no planning split.

approvedChanges.regressionPlan: Assert rendered assets always install bounded polling and EventSource error recovery; open the real event endpoint in the runtime test, append a valid trace event, and require a newer projected state without manual reload.
